tagline: Ski country down to the Vale of the Cross.
intro: NC 194 starts off US 19E near Cranberry, where one of the largest iron veins in the country made iron for the Confederate Army, and follows the Elk River up to Banner Elk, ski country, with Beech and Sugar mountains up the side roads. A short stretch of Old Turnpike Road joins the route there.

Past Banner Elk the road follows Craborchard Creek down into the Watauga valley at Valle Crucis, Latin for Vale of the Cross. The four miles from Banner Elk to the school at Valle Crucis are known for their curves, and trucks are sent around another way. The byway ends at US 321 in Vilas.

moments.title: Old Turnpike Road
moments.text: Neighbors paid their toll on this old game trail turned turnpike with six days' labor a year, and in the Civil War it smuggled escaped Union prisoners and Confederate draft dodgers over to Tennessee.

moments.title: Valle Crucis
moments.text: The Episcopal mission that names the byway ran a school here from 1895 until World War II, and Holy Cross Church, built in 1926, was modeled on a defunct medieval monastery in Wales.

moments.title: Mast General Store
moments.text: Henry Taylor built the store in 1882, the Mast family bought in and kept it three generations, and its slogan was "if you can't buy it here, you don't need it."

practical: Trucks are directed off NC 194 between Banner Elk and Valle Crucis onto a signed truck route.
